items.title: Collegium recommends Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Jammu & Kashmir High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Justice Bhati is currently a judge of the Rajasthan High Court. The decision to recommend his name for Chief Justice was taken by the collegium at a meeting held on August 31. If the Centre confirms the collegium's recommendation, Justice Bhati will take over as Chief Justice from Justice Sanjeev Kumar who has been serving as acting Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since June 2. Justice Bhati was a lawyer practicing across several areas of law for nearly 25 before he was elevated to the bench of the Rajasthan High Court on November 16, 2016. As a lawyer, he served as a Additional Advocate General for the State and was elected as President of the High Court Lawyers Association at different points Justice Bhati's wife, Justice Nupur Bhati, was also elevated as a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in 2023.

items.title: Collegium recommends Justice Krushna Ram Mohapatra as Chief Justice of Chhattisgarh High Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Krushna Ram Mohapatra , a judge of the Orissa High Court, as Chief Justice of the High Court of Chhattisgarh. The recommendation was made at a Collegium meeting held on August 6 and comes consequent upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice Ramesh Sinha on September 4. If the Centre confirms the Collegium's recommendation, Justice Mohapatra will take charge as Chief Justice of the Chhattisgarh High Court following the incumbent's retirement. Justice Mohapatra worked as Additional Standing Counsel for the State as well as the Orissa Public Service Commission, and served as advocate for entities including Central Cooperative Banks Limited (Keonjhar), the National Institute of Open Schooling under the Ministry of HRD, Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited, and Bank of Baroda. He was elevated as a judge of the Orissa High Court on April 17, 2015 where he has been serving till date.

items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The dismembered body of a 50-year-old woman who had been reported missing on August 22, was found packed in three sacks in two overhead water tanks of a house in Arisipalayam on Monday, August 31, in Tamil Nadu's Salem district. The deceased was identified as Thangamani, a resident of Balaji Colony in Thathanur in Mettupatti. She worked as a domestic worker at a house in Hasthampatti and had been reported missing at the Hasthampathi police station. The gruesome murder came to light after Ramesh (62), a temple priest residing in Arisipalayam, returned home with his wife Jamunarani and son Gautham after a two-day trip to Kumbakonam and Thanjavur. On opening a tap for domestic use, the family noticed a foul smell emanating from the water. According to reports, Ramesh and his son checked the two overhead water tanks on the terrace. items.summary: Argentina superstar Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international soccer on Monday, ending 21 years of national-team duty that were capped by winning the World Cup in 2022 to secure his place in the pantheon of the game's greatest ever players. "It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts deeply — but I understand that the time has come," the 39-year-old Messi said on his Instagram account. Messi, who will continue to play at club level with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer, played in a record-tying six World Cups. He won it four years ago in a tournament he dominated in Qatar and also led Argentina to the title match in 2014 and again this year, when the Albiceleste lost to Spain in extra time in New Jersey. Messi stands shoulder to shoulder with Diego Maradona, a compatriot with whom he was so often compared, and Brazil icon Pelé as the greatest players of all time. For many, he's the best. "I swear to you that I always gave it my all — not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too," Messi wrote.
